THE HIGH BOTHY. Three voices in the last warm room in the game. One is going down, one is a clerk from the Summit who walks down twice a week to be somewhere with people in it, and one is a child who is not going anywhere and has already decided she is.

NOBODY IN HERE ASKS THE PLAYER ANYTHING. A room that exists to be a rest should not have a job in it.

lines: Going down. Third time going down. It is not the Kin and it is not the cold.
It is that I keep getting to the bothy and being pleased I am at the bothy.
You are pleased you are at the bothy. Notice whether you want to stay.
I keep the standing list at the Summit. Three hundred and eleven names on it.
I walk down here twice a week for the noise. There is no noise up there at all.
You are on that list, by the way. Near the bottom. Everybody is near the bottom.
Mum says I can go up when I am sixteen. I am eleven.
I have already picked which ones. They do not know yet.
